# HAMS Task Recorder — Prototype Checkpoint

**Date:** 2026-06-12
**Branch:** `phase/push-reliability`
**Milestone:** 2-device pilot passed (manually configured units). Push reliability upgrade implemented.

---

## 1. Where the project is now

The app is a working prototype. A harvester can:

- Count FFB cuts fully offline (`+` / `−`), each press saving GPS + battery + timestamp to the phone.
- Have all saved data sent to Wialon automatically when validated Wi-Fi appears — even with the app closed or swiped away.
- Trigger a manual push with a 3-second button hold.

The 2-phone pilot (units pointed at Wialon by editing `local.properties` per build) succeeded end-to-end: GPS lock, counting, and push to Wialon all confirmed.

The current branch (`phase/push-reliability`) fixed the main field problem: on aggressive-OEM phones (Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi) auto-push used to silently fail until the app was reopened. A background-service Wi-Fi monitor now replaces the unreliable deferred job.

## 2. Fault tolerance — in plain words

### A cut is never lost
- The `+` button won't record without a GPS fix — no cut is ever saved "blind."
- If GPS freezes, a watchdog wakes it back up.
- Every press is written to the phone instantly, before anything else can fail.
- If the worker swipes the app away, the current task is saved immediately.

### Talking to the server safely
- Connections time out instead of hanging forever (5 s connect, 3 s read).
- The app understands every server reply (success, rejected, bad data, login refused, …) and reacts correctly.
- A broken connection is always closed cleanly.

### Sending in a smart order
- One good message → marked done, never sent twice.
- One bad message → set aside, the rest keep going.
- A dropped connection → wait and retry (30 s, 1 m, 2 m, 4 m, 5 m; up to 5 tries).
- Sends in small groups of 10, at most 10 tasks per round — a Wi-Fi drop loses only a little progress, not everything.
- Already-sent data is never re-sent; permanently-bad data is never retried forever.

### Making sure push actually fires (the main fix on this branch)
- A background service watches Wi-Fi directly, so push starts the moment good Wi-Fi appears — app closed or swiped.
- The service stays alive as long as unsent data exists.
- If the phone restarts the app from scratch, it checks for unsent data and pushes.
- No matter how often Wi-Fi flickers, the server is never flooded with duplicate jobs.

### Honest progress + no crashes
- The "X of N sent" counter stays correct even across multiple sending rounds.
- Any unexpected error retries later instead of crashing.

### Housekeeping
- A task left open overnight is closed automatically.
- Already-sent tasks are cleaned up after 30 days; unsent data is **never** deleted.
- An on-screen prompt asks the user to allow background running (stops aggressive phones from killing the app).

## 3. Fault tolerance — technical mapping (for developers)

| # | Mechanism | Tolerates |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | GPS gate — `+` gated on `GpsLockState.Locked` | Cut saved without coordinates |
| 2 | `LocationStream` watchdog single-shot poke | Stalled / cold-start-no-fix GPS stream |
| 3 | Synchronous Room insert on press | Process death between press and save |
| 4 | `onTaskRemoved` synchronous save | App swipe killing an active task |
| 5 | Connect 5 s / read 3 s timeouts | Indefinite socket hang |
| 6 | Typed `WialonError` mapping | Ambiguous server responses |
| 7 | `closeQuietly` on every failure path | Leaked sockets |
| 8 | Session kept open on per-frame reject, closed on transport fail | Wasting a live gateway / reusing a dead one |
| 9 | Per-event disposition (uploaded / rejected-continue / abort) | One bad row blocking a batch |
| 10 | Fail-fast on `#AL#0` / `#AL#01` | Pointless retries against unknown unit |
| 11 | Retry backoff 30/60/120/240/300 s ×5, re-fetch each attempt | Transient Wi-Fi / gateway flaps |
| 12 | Chunk size 10, fresh sender+login per chunk | One poisoned session spreading |
| 13 | `taskBatchLimit = 10` per worker run | Long backlog × Wi-Fi flap = large rollback |
| 14 | `WHERE pushed=0`, rejected=2 skipped | Double-send / infinite poison retry |
| 15 | `markTaskTerminalState` (uploaded vs failed); failed never auto-retried | Mislabeled completion |
| 16 | `WifiPushMonitor` (`registerNetworkCallback`) in FGS | OEM purge of deferred WorkManager job |
| 17 | Service survives `onTaskRemoved` while `pending>0` | Push dying on app swipe |
| 18 | WorkManager `UNMETERED` request | Cold-start (process fully dead) |
| 19 | `HamsApp.onCreate` start-service-if-pending | Recovery after process restart |
| 20 | Single dedup funnel `enqueueAuto(KEEP)` | Enqueue storm from flapping Wi-Fi |
| 21 | `PushCampaign` (SharedPreferences) + `resetIfStale` | Progress denominator reset across runs |
| 22 | Worker exceptions → `Result.retry()` | Crash loop |
| 23 | Terminal banner at separate notification id | `stopForeground(REMOVE)` wiping the banner |
| 24 | Daily rollover (init + 1 s tick) | Task left open across midnight |
| 25 | Retention purge 30 d; active/pending never purged | Storage bloat vs losing unsent work |
| 26 | Battery-optimisation onboarding | OEM background kills |

## 4. Accepted limitations (not bugs)

- **Force-stop** (user kills app from Settings) wipes the WorkManager queue and stops the service — push waits until the user reopens the app. Data is safe in SQLite; nothing is lost.
- **Reboot alone** does not restart a force-stopped app.
- **Phone hotspot / mobile data** never triggers auto-push — only validated unmetered Wi-Fi does (by design).
- **Self-cancelling +/− pairs** cause ~2 % report over-count in Wialon; SQLite stays truthful.
- **Blank IPS password** — any guessable `unique_id` could push fake data. Hardening deferred (CONTEXT.md "D-future").

## 5. Follow-on directions — status (resolved 2026-06-12)

Three scaling directions were worked through after the pilot:

- **Direction 1 — this checkpoint + fault tolerance.** ✅ **Closed** — captured in this document (sections 1–4).
- **Direction 2 — automated device → Wialon-unit provisioning.** 🔵 **Scoped, pending implementation.** One downloadable APK auto-claims a pre-created unit via an n8n broker + PostgreSQL; replaces editing `local.properties` per build. Decisions and open items tracked in `docs/HAMS_PROVISIONING_FINDINGS.md`.
- **Direction 3 — data push at scale.** ✅ **Closed — keep current mechanism.** No pool/relay, no rebuilt push engine. Wialon is fleet-grade and handles this load (lighter than the P99L hardware it replaces; each phone pushes to its own unit). Real deployment (~20 devices across estates, staggered times) is naturally spread — no thundering herd. Light improvements only: sensible heartbeat interval, optional jittered push-start, per-unit speed/distance filters = 0. **One vendor check (commercial, not technical):** confirm the Wialon plan's licensed-unit count + message/storage quota. The central-pool/relay option is documented as a "later, only if a single site proves it needs it" fallback in the Direction 2/scaling notes.
